slides.texte_overlay:
Things that make you
quietly attractive
Smell good, but only up close. One or two sprays, not a cloud. If people notice it when they hug you and not from across the room, you got it exactly right.
Keep your hands still. No fidgeting, no tapping on the table, no playing with your sleeves. Calm hands make you look relaxed, and relaxed is one of the most attractive things a person can be.
Be kind to the waiter. Thank them, look at them, learn their name. People watch how you treat someone who can't do anything for you, and they remember it far longer than your jokes.
Have a few things you really know about. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. You never lecture anyone, but when the topic comes up, you light up. Quiet depth is seriously attractive.
slides.texte_sophia: Have a few things you really know about. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. Quiet depth is seriously attractive.

slides.texte_overlay: Take care of your hands and your shoes. Clean nails, no cracked skin, shoes that aren't destroyed. Nobody says it out loud, but people notice the small details far more than the expensive ones.
Keep your phone in your pocket at dinner. Not on the table, not face down, not even once. Full attention is so rare now that it feels like a compliment without you saying a word.
Have a life you're excited about. A hobby, a project, a sport you're getting better at. People are drawn to someone who's going somewhere, not someone waiting for them to make his week.
